column1: prompt
Write a 600-word executive briefing arguing for investing in a company-wide AI upskilling program, targeting a skeptical CFO audience. Include ROI framing and risk mitigation.

Draft a competitive analysis memo comparing three cloud storage vendors (AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob) across cost, performance, compliance, and support. Recommend one for a healthcare startup.
Write a 500-word op-ed arguing that four-day work weeks increase productivity, targeting a mainstream business publication. Use three supporting studies and preempt the strongest counterargument.
Compose a fundraising appeal letter for a nonprofit that provides coding education to incarcerated people. Make the emotional and rational case simultaneously. 400–500 words.
Write the first chapter (600–800 words) of a near-future thriller where a whistleblower discovers that an AI system used for parole decisions has been deliberately manipulated.
Write a short story (500 words) told entirely through Slack messages between two colleagues who gradually realize they are working at competing companies on the same product.
Write a product review for a fictional kitchen gadget — The Sourdough Oracle — that is both earnestly helpful and subtly absurdist.

Write a post-mortem report for a production database outage that lasted 4 hours and affected 30,000 users. Cover timeline, root cause (a misconfigured migration), impact, and three systemic improvements.
Write a 500-word UX research report summarizing findings from 8 user interviews on a mobile banking app's onboarding flow. Identify top three pain points and recommend design changes.
Write a technical design document for a URL shortener service. Cover API design, database schema, hashing strategy, scalability considerations, and potential failure modes.

Draft a migration guide for engineering teams moving from REST to GraphQL. Cover schema design differences, query optimization, authentication changes, and common gotchas. Target audience: senior engineers.
Write a lesson plan for a 60-minute high school class on algorithmic bias. Include a warm-up activity, main lecture points, a case study discussion, and an exit ticket.
Write a 400-word explainer on how central banks use interest rate policy to manage inflation, suitable for a financially literate but non-economist audience.
Draft a company-wide AI usage policy covering acceptable use, data privacy rules, disclosure requirements when AI-generated content is published externally, and enforcement mechanisms.
Write a vendor due diligence questionnaire for assessing a third-party SaaS vendor's security posture. Include sections on data handling, SOC 2 compliance, incident response, and SLA terms.
Write a product requirements document (PRD) for a browser extension that summarizes any open browser tab on demand. Include user stories, non-goals, and success metrics.
Write a go-to-market strategy summary for a B2B SaaS tool that automates invoice reconciliation for accounting teams. Cover target segment, positioning, pricing model, and launch channels.
Write a 360-degree performance review guide for managers. Include instructions, sample questions for peers, direct reports, and self-assessment, plus guidance on avoiding recency and halo biases.
Draft a structured interview scorecard for evaluating candidates for a senior product manager role. Include five competencies, three questions per competency, and a 1–5 rubric.
Write a SWOT analysis narrative (not just a table) for a legacy newspaper entering the creator economy by launching a Substack-style subscription platform.
Draft a 12-month content strategy for a B2B cybersecurity company targeting CISOs. Cover content pillars, channel mix, cadence, and how to measure thought leadership impact.
Write a plain-English explanation of GDPR Article 17 (right to erasure) for a product team about to build a user data deletion feature.

Write the methodology section of a research proposal investigating the effect of sleep deprivation on decision-making quality among ICU nurses. Include study design, sample size justification, and ethical considerations.
Write a literature review outline (with paragraph-level summaries) on the economics of platform monopolies, covering at least five distinct scholarly arguments.
Write a month-long LinkedIn content calendar (20 posts) for a solo consultant specializing in supply chain resilience. Include post type, hook, and key message for each.
Write a crisis communication email to customers after a data breach exposed email addresses and hashed passwords. Strike the right legal, empathetic, and transparent tone. Include next steps.
Write a 500-word scene from a literary novel where two estranged siblings are forced to sort through their late mother's belongings. Show the tension without stating it directly.
Write an analogy-rich explanation of how transformer attention mechanisms work, targeting an ML engineer who knows Python but has never read the original paper.
Write a runbook for on-call engineers responding to a Redis cache eviction spike. Include diagnosis commands, escalation criteria, and rollback steps.
Write a board presentation narrative (not slides) summarizing a Series B startup's performance against OKRs, explaining two major misses without losing investor confidence.

Write a 600-word personal essay in first person from the perspective of a senior engineer who realizes their most successful open-source project has been used to build something harmful. Don't resolve the moral tension — let it breathe.

Write a comprehensive guide (700 words) on setting up observability for a microservices system: what to instrument, how to correlate logs/metrics/traces across services, alert fatigue pitfalls, and recommended tooling stack.

Write a 500-word case study of a B2B SaaS company's successful expansion from SMB to enterprise. Include the product changes required, go-to-market shift, pricing model evolution, and key lessons. Use realistic but fictional company details.
Write a 500-word argument that open-source AI models are better for society than proprietary ones. Acknowledge the strongest counterarguments. Target: a technically sophisticated general audience.
Write a 500-word explainer on how transformer neural networks work, targeted at a software engineer who understands Python and basic linear algebra but has not studied deep learning.

Write a comprehensive code review checklist for a team reviewing PRs on a Python backend service. Cover: correctness, security, performance, readability, testing, and documentation. Include examples of what 'good' and 'bad' look like for each.

Write a structured annotated bibliography of five real or plausible papers on the psychology of procrastination. For each, write a 100-word critical summary highlighting methodology strengths and limitations.
Write the opening scene of a screenplay set in a near-future immigration court where the judge is an AI system. The dialogue should establish moral complexity without taking sides. 500 words.

Write a pricing strategy memo for a developer tools startup moving from open-source freemium to a paid model. Cover: psychological pricing principles, tier design, community backlash mitigation, and revenue projections.

Write a plain-English guide for startup founders on the key differences between a SAFE note, a convertible note, and a priced equity round. Cover: mechanics, investor protections, dilution, and when each is appropriate.

Write a complete north star metric framework for a consumer social app. Define the north star metric, three input metrics, leading indicators for each, and explain how product decisions map to metric movement.
Write a technical explainer for a senior non-engineering leader on why migrating a monolith to microservices is risky, expensive, and often the wrong choice — and what to consider before committing.

Write a 600-word short story that takes place entirely in a company's Slack workspace during an all-hands gone wrong. Use channel names, emoji reactions, and message formatting as part of the narrative structure.

Write an interactive Socratic dialogue (600 words) between a professor and a student that leads the student to discover the concept of opportunity cost on their own, without the professor ever naming it.

Write a 500-word board memo recommending the acquisition of a smaller competitor for their engineering talent and IP rather than their revenue. Address valuation rationale, integration risk, and retention strategy.

Write a compensation philosophy document for a 100-person tech startup. Cover: benchmarking methodology, equity vs. cash trade-offs, geographic pay adjustments, pay transparency approach, and annual review cadence.

Write a guide (600 words) on designing for failure in distributed systems. Cover: idempotency, circuit breakers, bulkheads, chaos engineering, and graceful degradation — with concrete code-adjacent examples for each concept.
Write a 500-word speech for a high school commencement arguing that the most important skill graduates will need is the ability to change their minds gracefully. Make it specific, not generic.

Write a medium-length analysis (600 words) of why subscription business models fail: common failure patterns, the metrics that mask problems, and what a sustainable subscription looks like vs. a leaky bucket.

Write the user research synthesis document for a food delivery app that interviewed 12 users about their pain points. Present themes, supporting quotes (fictional), jobs-to-be-done, and design implications.

Write a quarterly engineering health report for a CTO. Cover: deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR, team morale proxy (optional PTO usage), tech debt ratio, and recommended investments.
Write a 500-word explanation of game theory's Nash equilibrium using the prisoner's dilemma, extended to explain how this concept applies to corporate price wars and arms races. Target: MBA students.

Write a 500-word monologue by a data scientist who discovers that the model they built to predict employee attrition is being used to fire people preemptively, not to retain them. Interior voice, not a speech.

Write a competitor teardown (600 words) of Notion from the perspective of a startup that builds a competing tool. Cover product strengths, weaknesses, customer pain points, pricing vulnerabilities, and strategic openings.

Write a guide to semantic versioning (semver) for a team that has been releasing without a versioning strategy. Cover the spec, when to bump major/minor/patch, pre-release tags, and a worked example of a breaking change migration.
Write a responsible disclosure policy for a tech company's bug bounty program. Cover: scope, severity definitions, response SLAs, reward ranges, legal safe harbor, and what qualifies as out-of-scope.
Write a 500-word primer on marginal cost vs. average cost for a product manager who needs to understand when building one more feature is worth it from an economic perspective.

Write a 600-word analysis of the classic innovator's dilemma as it applies to an incumbent cloud database vendor facing a startup offering serverless, usage-based pricing. What should the incumbent do?

Write a literature review (600 words) synthesizing research on the effectiveness of spaced repetition for long-term memory retention. Cover at least four studies, note methodological limitations, and conclude with practical implications.
Write the Wikipedia article for a fictional startup that 'disrupted' the municipal water infrastructure space, including a controversy section about its collapse. Dry encyclopedic tone throughout.

Write a comprehensive guide to designing idempotent APIs. Define idempotency precisely, explain why it matters for distributed systems, cover implementation patterns (idempotency keys, conditional requests, upsert semantics), common pitfalls, and how to test for idempotency. Target: API designers with 2–5 years experience.

Write a vendor scorecard and evaluation framework for selecting a cloud data warehouse (Snowflake vs. BigQuery vs. Redshift vs. Databricks). Include: 10 evaluation criteria with weights, scoring rubric, and a worked example comparing two finalists.

Write a 500-word flash fiction story where the protagonist is an AI assistant who gradually realizes the 'user' they have been helping for six months is another AI testing social engineering techniques. No genre clichés — make it feel literary.

Write a 500-word explainer on the CAP theorem for a senior engineer who has never built distributed systems. Use a concrete analogy, cover all three properties, explain what real databases actually choose, and debunk common misconceptions.

Write a strategic analysis of the 'build vs. buy vs. partner' decision for a healthcare startup that needs a medical records integration layer. Cover: total cost of ownership, time-to-market, IP control, compliance risk, and vendor dependency risk. Recommend a path.

Write a plain-English explanation of what due diligence means in a Series A funding round from the startup's perspective: what documents are requested, what red flags investors look for, how to prepare, and common deal-killers.

Write a product strategy memo for a B2C app that has hit a growth ceiling at 500K MAU. The memo should diagnose why growth has plateaued (using fictional but plausible data), identify three strategic options, and recommend one with clear reasoning.

Write a competitive landscape analysis report for a VC firm evaluating the AI-powered legal research market. Cover: key players, differentiation, pricing models, go-to-market strategies, defensibility, and market size estimate.

Write a manager's guide to conducting a layoff conversation. Include: preparation steps, exact language to use at the start of the conversation, what not to say, how to handle emotional reactions, and what to communicate to the remaining team afterward.

Write a 500-word scene from a novel set in a fictional mid-2030s Bengaluru where delivery drones and auto-rickshaws share airspace, and a retired traffic cop becomes the city's first 'sky warden.' Ground it in specific sensory and cultural detail.

Write an API design review checklist for REST APIs. Cover: URL naming conventions, HTTP method semantics, status code correctness, pagination design, error response format, versioning strategy, backward compatibility, rate limiting headers, and documentation completeness.

Write a 500-word primer on tokenomics for a software engineer who has never studied crypto. Explain token supply mechanics, inflation/deflation, token utility vs. speculative value, and why most token models fail.

Write a 500-word case for why engineering teams should invest time in internal developer tools and platform engineering, aimed at convincing a skeptical VP of Engineering focused on shipping product features.
Write a 500-word critical analysis of the methodology of a hypothetical study claiming that meditation apps reduce anxiety as measured by GAD-7 scores. Identify at least five methodological concerns.

Write a memo recommending the sunset of a product feature used by only 3% of customers but consuming 20% of infrastructure costs. Address: user impact mitigation, migration path, customer communication strategy, and expected savings.

Write a 500-word piece of literary journalism about a fictional competitive prompt engineering championship. Capture the tension, the subculture, and one contestant's internal monologue during the final round.

Write a comprehensive guide on database indexing strategy for a senior developer audience. Cover: B-tree vs hash indexes, composite index key ordering, partial indexes, covering indexes, index bloat, and when NOT to index.

Write a 500-word explainer on what 'entropy' means in information theory (Shannon entropy), how it differs from thermodynamic entropy, and why it is the right measure for compression algorithms and model uncertainty.

Write a 500-word internal memo arguing against rewriting the company's core backend service from Ruby on Rails to Go. Address the argument that Go is faster, counter with total cost of ownership, migration risk, and team expertise.
Write a technical blog post (600–800 words) explaining the difference between REST and GraphQL APIs. Include a code snippet example for each. Target audience: junior developers.
Write a migration guide for teams moving from Webpack 4 to Vite. Cover configuration differences, common issues, and performance expectations.
Write an internal engineering wiki page explaining how your team uses feature flags in production, including rollout strategy and rollback procedure.
Write a competitive analysis section for a business plan comparing your project management SaaS against Asana, Monday.com, and Notion. Focus on pricing, integrations, and target segment differences.
Draft a business case memo arguing for increasing the customer success team headcount from 3 to 6. Include cost-benefit framing and expected impact on churn.
Write a go-to-market strategy summary for launching a B2B HR software product in Southeast Asia. Address channel, pricing, and localization.
Write a persuasive op-ed (500 words) arguing that remote work permanently improves software engineering productivity, using data-backed claims.
Write a grant proposal introduction section for a nonprofit applying for funding to run digital literacy programs in rural communities.
Write a lesson plan for a 60-minute introductory workshop on machine learning for non-technical marketing professionals. Include learning objectives, activities, and materials.
Write an explainer article on how transformer models work for a technically literate but non-ML-specialist audience. Use analogies, not equations.
Write a post-mortem report for a production database outage that lasted 4 hours due to a failed migration script. Include timeline, root cause, and prevention steps.
Write a user research synthesis report based on interviews with 8 users of a mobile banking app. Themes: navigation confusion, trust concerns, and feature requests.
Write the first chapter (600 words) of a near-future thriller where an AI model begins flagging its own outputs as potentially dangerous.
Write a fictional internal memo from a fictional company where the AI assistant has been given budget approval authority and the finance team is reacting.
Write a company AI usage policy covering acceptable use, data privacy, output review requirements, and prohibited use cases. Tone: professional, not legalese.
Draft a social media policy for employees at a publicly traded company, covering what they can/cannot post about work.
